items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There was a restaurant and poolroom near where we lived which was owned by a man named Rick and we ate there on credit and paid him the same as we did grandma when things were going alright.

ctx.x: Frank Newton and I roomed together and he became the sweetheart of Wilhelmina and ate with the family. Dickie Wells, Mack Walker, Harold McFerran, John William and myself ate in restaurants. Hubert Mann was married to a Springfield girl and lived with her family.

The band was not getting much work so Grandma Jackson let us stay with her and when we did get a job or some jobs, we would pay her the back rent. There was a restaurant and poolroom near where we lived which was owned by a man named Rick and we ate there on credit and paid him the same as we did grandma when things were going alright. Neither Rick nor Grandma worried about their money if we were three weeks or more behind in our rent or eating bills.

We had plenty of time to rehearse and we did so everyday. We would play a popular number taking the first chorus as it was written on the orchestration, sometimes leaving the introduction as it was, or giving it another intro. Then we would all think of an idea to put in certain places. If the idea was good, it stayed. If not, we would pull some other ideas until we had the number sounding the way we wanted it.
